glosses: To cut.

examples.text: My good blade carves the casques of men, / My tough lance thrusteth sure, / My strength is as the strength of ten, / Because my heart is pure.

glosses: To cut meat in order to serve it.

examples.text: You carve the roast and I’ll serve the vegetables.

glosses: To shape to sculptural effect; to produce (a work) by cutting, or to cut (a material) into a finished work, especially with cuts that are curved rather than only straight slices.

examples.text: to carve a name into a tree
The facades of the buildings fronting upon the avenue within the wall were richly carven[…].

The half-dozen pieces […] were painted white and carved with festoons of flowers, birds and cupids. To display them the walls had been tinted a vivid blue which had now faded, but the carpet, which had evidently been stored and recently relaid, retained its original turquoise.

glosses: To perform a series of turns without pivoting, so that the tip and tail of the snowboard take the same path.

examples.text: […] who could easily have carved themselves their own food.

glosses: To lay out; to contrive; to design; to plan.

examples.text: Lie ten nights awake carving the fashion of a new doublet.
